The supplied papers do address RL self-play for strategy games, especially board and adversarial games. One paper trains a transformer with plain policy-gradient self-play on Generals.io and reaches superhuman play [1]. Another adapts AlphaZero-style self-play to the asymmetric game Tablut using separate policy and value heads plus stabilization techniques [2]. A third uses self-play reinforcement learning and test-time search to reach superhuman Stratego play and also applies the approach to Barrage Stratego, Hanabi, and dou dizhu [3].

If you want the closest match to “rl self play strategy games,” [1], [2], and [3] are the most directly relevant; [1] is a real-time strategy game, [2] is an asymmetric board game, and [3] focuses on hidden-information strategy games.
